name: John
description: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament

points: He is transfigured before Peter, James and John, and there appear unto them Elias with Moses, talking with him.

note.label: Mark 9: The Transfiguration, the Dumb Spirit, and Who Shall Be Greatest

points: John reports one casting out devils in his name who followed not them, and is told, Forbid him not: for he that is not against us is on our part.

note.label: Mark 9: The Transfiguration, the Dumb Spirit, and Who Shall Be Greatest

points: And as he sat upon the mount of Olives over against the temple, Peter and James and John and Andrew asked him privately, Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign when all these things shall be fulfilled? Their question was: when will this temple be destroyed, when shall the end come?

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

points: John reports one casting out devils in his name whom they forbade, because he followed not with them.

note.label: Luke 9: The Twelve Sent, the Confession, and the Cost of Following

points: The Samaritan village would not receive him, and James and John ask to command fire to come down from heaven.

note.label: Luke 9: The Twelve Sent, the Confession, and the Cost of Following

points: Peter and John are sent to prepare the passover. Christ kept the passover, and a follower of Christ keeps what he kept.

note.label: Luke 22: The Passover, the Betrayal, and the Denial

points: Peter and John go up to the temple at the hour of prayer, being the ninth hour. Counting the way the scripture counts, the day starts at six in the morning: six is the start, so the third hour is nine in the morning, the sixth hour is noon, and the ninth hour is three in the afternoon. Write that down, because knowing how the hours are counted keeps you from being confused later.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

points: All the people see him walking and praising the Most High, know he is the one who sat for alms at the Beautiful gate, and are filled with wonder, running together to Peter and John at the porch called Solomon's. Notice it says "all the people," because a book establishes its characters at the start and then speaks in pronouns, "he," "she," "they," "all," without re-naming the people every time.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

points: Now when they saw the boldness of Peter and John. They saw the boldness of Peter. And John. So Peter was not the only one rolling like Christ. Peter and John.

note.label: I Need More Confidence

points: When they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and perceived that they were unlearned and ignorant men, they marvelled and took knowledge of them that they had been with Jesus. The rulers saw these men were not slick, cunning, and crafty like themselves; they were bold, coming as if straight off a plantation and a field, not the regular church men. That boldness is the natural animation of the Holy Spirit, not something you force or make up.

note.label: Acts 4: The Stone the Builders Rejected

points: When the apostles at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of the Most High, they sent Peter and John, who prayed for them that they might receive the Holy Ghost. Notice the order: Philip, the deacon, woke up the city and planted, but the apostles had to come and put the spirit on them. It is the same order today, where the bishop and the apostles visit the cities where new schools open and pray over the congregation.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

points: James, Cephas, and John gave Paul and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship; that we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision. The heathen: talking about the northern kingdom.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

points: They saw that the gospel of the uncircumcision was committed unto me, as the gospel of the circumcision was unto Peter, for he that wrought effectually in Peter to the apostleship of the circumcision, the same was mighty in me toward the Gentiles. Christ worked in Peter toward the Jews born and raised in the law and circumcised the eighth day, and the same Christ worked in Paul toward the dispersed. James, Cephas, and John gave the right hands of fellowship that we should go unto the heathen and they unto the circumcision, remembering the poor.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

points: The revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave unto him to show unto his servants: John bore record of all things that he saw. Christ had to leave his image recorded for us in these last days, because in the last days they would come preaching another Jesus.

note.label: Puerto Rico: The Flame Of Resistance

points: “and he sent and signified it by his angel unto his servant John:”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 1 A Visit From The Lord

points: John writes to the seven churches in Asia, meaning Asia Minor above the Mediterranean Sea, not China. Grace and peace come from the one who is, was and is to come, and from the seven Spirits before his throne. Those seven Spirits correspond to the menorah: angels before the throne, burning like its lamps.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 4 Kingdom Vision

points: “John to the seven churches which are in Asia:” Write this down: Asia Minor. You got Asia in terms of China, then you got Asia in terms of Asia Minor, which is around the Mediterranean Sea. Acts 6:9 has men of Asia disputing with Stephen; in Acts 16 the Holy Ghost forbade Paul to preach the word in Asia at that time, and later, in Acts 19, Paul had turned away much people throughout all Asia; by 1 Corinthians 16 there were churches of Asia. The Lord will sometimes block your way from certain regions, certain countries, certain states: don't go there, there's nobody there yet, I want you to go here. We got to do things in God's time.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 1 A Visit From The Lord

points: “I John, who also am your brother, and companion in tribulation, and in the kingdom and patience of Jesus Christ, was in the isle that is called Patmos,” Patmos is a little island in the Aegean Sea, shaped like a seahorse. John of Patmos, also called John the Revelator, John the Divine, John the Theologian, is the John of Revelation, the apocalyptic text forming the final book of the New Testament. By most biblical historians he is considered exiled there as a result of anti-Christian persecution under the Roman emperor Domitian. Anti-Christian meaning what? Anti-Israelites keeping the commandments. Domitian was related to Titus and Vespasian, the younger brother of Titus, and he became emperor; that dude was wicked as hell. Since the Roman era, Christians and historians have considered the writer of Revelation to be the apostle John, John the Evangelist, supposed author of the Gospel of John.

Early tradition says John was banished to Patmos by the Roman authorities, and it is credible because banishment was a common punishment used during the imperial period for offenses like magic and astrology, and prophecy was viewed by the Romans as belonging to the same category. So Rome considered any type of prophecy in the same category as magic and astrology. Prophecy with political implications like John's in Revelation would have been perceived as a threat to Roman political power and order: Rome had its ten hills and ten allies supporting it, like America today with the ten common markets, so they figured this is against Rome, we have to exile this guy. Three of the islands in the Sporades were places where political offenders were banished. According to Tertullian, John was banished to Patmos after being plunged into boiling oil in Rome and suffering nothing from it: they threw him in boiling oil to kill him and he didn't die. It is said that all in the audience of the Colosseum were converted upon witnessing this miracle, in the late first century during the reign of Domitian.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 1 A Visit From The Lord

points: John was exiled on the island of Patmos. Look at its location in relation to Asia Minor: the seven churches were in that region of the Greek empire, where our people had been scattered. Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamos, Thyatira and the other churches were Israelite congregations in those settlements. That history and geography come before reading the messages to their leaders.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 2 Message to the 7 Churches

points: “And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband”: in 2 Esdras 9 the prophet Ezra saw a vision of a woman who transformed into new Jerusalem, and that is what this verse makes reference to. This city Jerusalem refers to the people, first and foremost.
